newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Bicycle to report flat net for '96.
newsitem.headline: China Bicycle to report flat net for '96.

text.p: Net earnings of the Shenzhen-based China Bicycle Holdings Co Ltd for 1996 would roughly equal the previous year's level of 51.25 million yuan, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The firm sold over 1.1 million bicycles last year compared with 1.3 million in 1995 and 1.6 million a year earlier, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
About 500,000 bicycles were sold to the U.S. in 1996 compared with 700,000 in 1995, the official said, adding that lower overseas sales resulted from U.S. anti-dumping charges.

Washington earlier charged China Bicycle was dumping its products in the U.S. market. After a year-long investigation, U.S. trade officials said in June 1996 they had decided not to impose sanctions on Chinese bicycle manufacturers.

"The firm saw a gradual recovery in its business since last June and expects its sales to reach the 1994 level this year," the official said. The company sold 1.66 million bicycles in 1994, with 1.2 million exported.

China Bicycle reported net profits of 8.58 million yuan in January-June, 1996, down from 72.53 million yuan in the first half of 1995 due to the U.S. anti-dumping charges. China Bicycle reported after-tax profits of 137.21 million yuan for 1994.
